source: i want to build a avatar catalog editor like game where users can choose a avatar outfit from the avatar shops in the experience.

image_prompt.text: A central oversized gathering hub between the avatar shops, sized to hold a crowd of browsing avatars
Detailed spots built as backdrops for showing off a newly picked outfit
A distinct structure visible across the shopping area so players can navigate by sight
Avatar outfit shops players go inside to browse and choose from

notes: Static Settlement was chosen because personalization here happens entirely through the avatar and never through property - the genre file names this case exactly.
The core loop is a catalog UI. Layout can only supply the room it happens in.
Enterable shops carry P3; if the shops are storefront kiosks instead, this drops to P0.

open_questions.ask: No look was stated - bright modern retail, or something more stylized?
Do players walk inside each shop, or browse from an open storefront? Interiors are a slower build.

coverage_missing.ask: No look was stated - bright modern retail, or something more stylized?
Do players walk inside each shop, or browse from an open storefront?
Is there a mirror or preview spot where the chosen outfit gets shown off, or is it all in the menu?

answers.ask: No look was stated - bright modern retail, or something more stylized?
answers.answer: Use a bright modern retail look, like a clean avatar fashion mall.

answers.ask: Do players walk inside each shop, or browse from an open storefront? Interiors are a slower build.
answers.answer: Use open storefronts for browsing; keep the shops simple and easy to access.
